rules.rule_en: An idiom (also called idiomatic expression) is an expression, word or phrase that has a figurative meaning conventionally understood by native speakers. This meaning is different from the literal meaning of the idiom's individual elements.
Given below are some idiomatic expressions with their meanings. Understand the meaning.
A phrase is a group of words that forms a meaningful unit, but it is not a complete sentence. In other words, it does not have a subject or a verb.
Idioms derived from boxing terminology used to describe general life situations.
Replace the words in italics with the appropriate idioms, making suitable changes wherever necessary.
An idiom is an expression in English language that has a special meaning of its own. It cannot be understood from the meanings of the individual words.
An idiom is an expression in English with a special meaning of its own.
